causalMechanism.primaryVector: Microvascular and fibrotic vascular sequence: in service-connected systemic sclerosis, endothelial injury with intimal proliferation and progressive obliterative vasculopathy narrows the digital arteries and arterioles, while platelet activation, increased endothelin-1 and reduced nitric oxide and prostacyclin signaling shift the digital vascular bed toward vasoconstriction and impaired vasodilation. The consequence is an exaggerated, reversible digital vasospasm in response to cold or emotional stress — Raynaud's phenomenon — which in systemic sclerosis is not a benign primary disorder but a marker and driver of progressive digital ischemia; when the vasospasm and fixed structural narrowing coexist, persistent hypoperfusion produces digital pitting scars, ischemic ulcers, and auto-amputation of fingertips. Hughes et al. (PMID 32099191) state that Raynaud phenomenon occurs in virtually all patients with systemic sclerosis and is often the earliest clinical manifestation, and that it is caused by impaired digital perfusion requiring careful assessment. Sunderkötter and Riemekasten (PMID 16987831) describe Raynaud's phenomenon in systemic sclerosis as an initial event in the pathophysiological cascade leading to sclerosis, characterized by recurrent reversible spasms of small arterioles and digital arteries triggered by cold and emotional stress and producing the characteristic sudden pallor of the digits. Maciejewska et al. (PMID 35566614) review Raynaud's phenomenon with a focus on systemic sclerosis and state that systemic sclerosis is one of the most frequent causes of secondary Raynaud's phenomenon and that its appearance may occur long before other signs and symptoms, emphasizing the treatment distinction between primary and secondary forms. Framing under 38 CFR § 3.310: this is a § 3.310(a) direct-causation theory — the service-connected systemic sclerosis is asserted to have produced a separate, separately rated vascular condition, secondary Raynaud's phenomenon, with its own diagnostic code at DC 7117 rather than being folded into the skin or musculoskeletal evaluation of the scleroderma itself. It is not a § 3.310(b) aggravation theory; an aggravation theory would be required only where the record shows pre-existing primary Raynaud's disease (DC 7124) or cold-injury-related vasospasm and the claim is that the systemic sclerosis measurably worsened a baseline vasospastic disorder, in which case the attributable increment must be separated from the natural progression of the primary disease and § 3.310(b) governs. Chronology and the individual analysis under § 3.310(a) or (b) require documented systemic sclerosis with American College of Rheumatology or EULAR classification features (for example, sclerodactyly, specific autoantibodies, nailfold capillary abnormalities, or internal-organ involvement), a clinical description of characteristic attacks meeting the DC 7117 note definition — sequential digital color change lasting minutes to hours, precipitated by cold or emotional stress — and a temporal relationship in which the vasospastic attacks begin with or after disease onset. Where digital ulcers or auto-amputation are asserted for the 60 or 100 percent tiers, the ulcer history and imaging or photographic documentation must be of record. Only then can an examiner state that the Raynaud's syndrome is at least as likely as not caused by the service-connected systemic sclerosis — a conclusion requiring documented chronology, accounted-for competing causes, and an approximate balance of evidence consistent with § 3.102. Competing causes that must be excluded or weighed include primary Raynaud's disease (which is the schedule's separate DC 7124 entity), cold-injury residuals under DC 7122 (whose note directs separate evaluation of Raynaud's syndrome unless those findings already support an evaluation there), cigarette smoking and other vasoconstrictor exposure, beta-blocker, ergotamine, or stimulant medication, hypothyroidism, carpal tunnel syndrome and thoracic outlet syndrome, vibration-tool exposure, cryoglobulinemia, and other connective tissue diseases such as mixed connective tissue disease or systemic lupus erythematosus, which are distinct service-connected or non-service-connected identities and must not be merged with systemic sclerosis. No individual probability is asserted here. Rating discipline under § 4.14: DC 7117 evaluations are for Raynaud's syndrome as a whole, so the same digital attacks, ulcers, or amputations may not be compensated a second time under the cold-injury code or as residuals of the scleroderma skin evaluation, and separate amputation ratings follow only the amputation rule and the schedule's own provisions.

Primary condition: Service-connected systemic sclerosis (scleroderma), with documented cutaneous or visceral involvement
Primary diagnostic-code proposal: 38 CFR § 4.118, DC 7821 (cutaneous manifestations of collagen-vascular diseases not listed elsewhere (including scleroderma, calcinosis cutis, subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, and dermatomyositis)) — evaluated under the General Rating Formula for the Skin; visceral involvement is separately rated in the affected body system, for example esophageal disease under § 4.114
Secondary condition: Raynaud's syndrome (secondary Raynaud's phenomenon with digital vasospasm, and its digital ulcer and auto-amputation sequelae) in a veteran with service-connected systemic sclerosis
Secondary diagnostic-code proposal: 38 CFR § 4.104, DC 7117 (Raynaud's syndrome (also known as secondary Raynaud's phenomenon or secondary Raynaud's)): 100 percent with two or more digital ulcers plus auto-amputation of one or more digits and a history of characteristic attacks; 60 percent with two or more digital ulcers and history of characteristic attacks; 40 percent for characteristic attacks occurring at least daily; 20 percent for attacks four to six times a week; 10 percent for attacks one to three times a week; with the note that these evaluations are for Raynaud's syndrome as a whole regardless of the number of extremities involved. DC 7124 governs primary Raynaud's disease only and must not be used here. Qualified-human rating review required
Original nexus theory: Causation

Legal boundary: § 3.310(a) concerns proximate causation; § 3.310(b) concerns attributable worsening beyond natural progression against a qualifying baseline. The at least as likely as not standard requires individual evidence and competing causes to be weighed. Apply claim-period rating criteria and § 4.14 nonpyramiding.
